panels.label: Steering
panels.description: Lateral control, lane changes, and steering behavior

items.title: Enable Modular Assistive Driving System (MADS)
items.description: Enable MADS. Disable toggle to revert back to stock sunnypilot engagement/disengagement.

items.title: Use enhanced Rivian MADS
items.description: Adds to MADS on Rivian: one click up on the stalk turns steering assist on or off, every brake mode can be chosen, shifting into Park or Reverse or a full stalk pull switches MADS off, and a minimum speed to engage can be set. When off, MADS works as in stock sunnypilot: the brake turns steering assist off and it comes back with cruise.

items.title: Toggle with Main Cruise
items.description: Note: For vehicles without LFA/LKAS button, disabling this will prevent lateral control engagement.

items.title: Unified Engagement Mode (UEM)
items.description: Engage lateral and longitudinal control with cruise control engagement. Note: Once lateral control is engaged via UEM, it will remain engaged until it is manually disabled via the MADS button or car shut off.

items.title: Steering Mode on Brake Pedal
items.description: Choose how Automatic Lane Centering (ALC) behaves after the brake pedal is manually pressed in sunnypilot.

items.title: Minimum Speed to Engage MADS
items.description: Minimum vehicle speed required to (re-)engage MADS lateral control. In Pause mode this also applies to resuming after the brake is released, so steering assist comes back once the car reaches this speed. 0 = no minimum.

sections.title: Lane Centering
sections.description: Keep the car in its lane. One of Lane Centering, Lane Guard or Blendful (FM Pilot)

items.title: Lane Centering
items.description: FM Pilot - pick one way of keeping the car in its lane, or Off for the driving model alone. Lane Centering (AdventurePilot): keeps the car in the middle of the painted lane instead of wherever the driving model chooses to sit; only acts when both lane lines are clearly visible (unless One-Line Mode is on), and steps aside for lane changes and turn signals. Lane Guard: a gentle correction only when the planned path brings the body too close to a lane line or road edge; pauses while you steer or signal (from gerrylum's rx-wb). Blendful (alpha): a gentle nudge toward the lane center on top of the model's own steering, stronger when the lane lines are clear; yields around obstacles, works down to about 1 mph (0.3 m/s), off during turns and lane changes; draws its blue center line. Needs a custom (non-Default) model (from sunnypilot).
items.details:
Lane Centering's corrections are deliberately small and are smoothed in over about half a second, so this should
read as the car sitting straighter rather than as active steering. Whenever the lane lines become unreliable, a
lane change starts or a turn signal comes on, the correction fades away rather than being dropped in one go.
Only one of the three can be on at a time.

items.title: Position in Lane
items.description: Sit deliberately off the middle of the lane. Positive values sit to the right, negative to the left. The car is never aimed closer than 1.1 m/3.6 ft to either line, so a large offset in a narrow lane is trimmed back.

items.title: Centering Strength
items.description: Sets how hard the car is pulled back toward the middle of the lane. Higher means it sits closer to the middle but works harder to get there. 0.6 suits the cars and roads tested so far. Lower feels smoother than it really is, and 0.3 is too weak to hold against a road crown, leaving the car sitting off center all day.

items.title: Close Enough To Center
items.description: How far off the middle of the lane the car is allowed to sit before lane centering does anything about it. Smaller sits closer to the middle. It does not make the car calmer. A wide tolerance lets the car drift to the edge and get kicked back, which reverses more often, not less. Road testing settled on 0.02. The car's own screen shows this in cm/in.

items.title: Let the Model Sit Off Center
items.description: How much freedom the driving model keeps to sit well off the middle of the lane when it is sure of itself, which usually means it is avoiding something. 1.0 always lets it have its way, 0 centers the car regardless. This only applies to large departures; small ones are always corrected.

items.title: One-Line Mode
items.description: When only one lane line is clearly visible, such as on an on-ramp with a faded edge line or a town street with a center line and a bare curb, keep the car from sitting too close to that line. It only ever moves the car away from the visible line, never past the middle of the lane, and not at all when it cannot see anything on the other side.
items.details:
Experimental. It never aims at a lane middle it cannot see. Anything the driving model is unsure of on the far side,
such as a faint line or the edge of the tarmac, can only make the move smaller. It does not follow a line that
bends away from the car's path, such as the line at a highway exit. Position in Lane and Let the Model Sit Off Center
do not apply in this mode.

items.title: One-Line Mode, Distance From an Edge Line
items.description: How far One-Line Mode keeps the car from a visible line at the edge of the road. 1.5 is the car's normal position in a lane. Smaller sits closer to the line, larger moves further away from it. These are the driving model's own distances, not a measured gap between tire and paint.

items.title: One-Line Mode, Distance From a Center or Lane Line
items.description: How far One-Line Mode keeps the car from a visible center line or line between lanes. 1.5 is the car's normal position in a lane. Smaller sits closer to the line, larger moves further away from it. When it cannot tell which kind of line it is, the smaller of the two distances is used.

items.title: Show Correction On Screen
items.description: Draws a small bar while driving showing which way lane centering is nudging the car and how hard. The bar fills to the side the car is being pulled, stays dim while the car is already close enough to the middle, and turns gray when the lane lines cannot be trusted. While One-Line Mode is keeping the car clear of a single line the bar turns light blue, a mark at its end shows which side that line is on, and the screen says "one line".

sections.title: Blinker Control
sections.description: Lateral pause behavior during turn signals

items.title: Pause Lateral Control with Blinker
items.description: Pause lateral control with blinker when traveling below the desired speed selected.

sub_items.title: Minimum Speed to Pause Lateral Control
Post-Blinker Delay
sub_items.description: Delay before lateral control resumes after the turn signal ends.

sections.title: Torque Control
sections.description: Steering torque tuning and lateral control method

items.title: Enforce Torque Lateral Control
items.description: Enable this to enforce sunnypilot to steer with Torque lateral control.

items.title: Lateral Jerk Torque Controller
items.description: Looks ahead at planned steering to reduce sudden corrections, so the wheel moves more smoothly through turns. Works with Self-Tune and custom tuning. Thanks to @twilsonco for the implementation.

items.title: Self-Tune
items.description: Enables self-tune for Torque lateral control for platforms that do not use Torque lateral control by default.

items.title: Less Restrict Settings for Self-Tune (Beta)
items.description: Less strict settings when using Self-Tune. This allows torqued to be more forgiving when learning values.

items.title: Enable Custom Tuning
items.description: Enables custom tuning for Torque lateral control. Modifying Lateral Acceleration Factor and Friction below will override the offline values indicated in the YAML files within "opendbc/car/torque_data". The values will also be used live when "Manual Real-Time Tuning" toggle is enabled.

items.title: Manual Real-Time Tuning
items.description: Enforces the torque lateral controller to use the fixed values instead of the learned values from Self-Tune. Enabling this toggle overrides Self-Tune values.

items.title: Torque Control Tune Version
items.description: Select the version of Torque Control Tune to use.

sections.title: Lane Change
sections.description: Automatic lane change timing and behavior

items.title: Auto Lane Change by Blinker
items.description: Set a timer to delay the auto lane change operation when the blinker is used. No nudge on the steering wheel is required to auto lane change if a timer is set. Default is Nudge.
items.details: Please use caution when using this feature. Only use the blinker when traffic and road conditions permit.

items.title: Block Lane Change: Road Edge Detection
items.description: Blocks lane change when the model sees a road edge on the side you signal.

items.title: Auto Lane Change: Delay with Blind Spot
items.description: Toggle to enable a delay timer for lane changes when blind spot monitoring (BSM) detects a vehicle in your blind spot.

sections.title: FM Custom Torque Settings
sections.description: FM Pilot - how much steering torque openpilot may use on the Rivian and how it backs off when you steer

items.title: Max Torque
items.description: 385 = stock AP. The most steering torque openpilot may use under about 20 mph, tapering back to the usual limits by about 38 mph; highway limits are unchanged. The panda's limit follows this number. Above 385 openpilot also lets torque build faster under 25 mph and uses the full limit past 90° of steering wheel, and it only reaches for the extra torque when the usual limit runs out. Overriding takes a firmer hand as the number rises: under about 22 mph your steering fully cancels openpilot's torque at about 2.9 Nm at 385, 3.4 Nm at 475 and 3.9 Nm at 580 (the driver-torque rule is unchanged; it scales with the limit). Only changes in off-road mode and applies from the next drive.

items.title: Release Guard
items.description: When you hold the wheel tighter than openpilot wants in a slow turn, openpilot's correction pushes back against your hands, and that push is still there when you let go, so the wheel can swing past center. Release Guard limits that push against you while you steer into the turn under 15 mph (fading out by 20 mph), and fades out over 0.5 s after you let go. Stock = off. 150 = at most 150 counts against you, 75 = at most 75. Never touches feedforward or any torque limit; off with Lateral Jerk or NNLC.

sections.title: Feedforward Settings
sections.description: FM Pilot - extra steering torque for the wheel angle a slow turn needs, per side

items.title: Low-Speed Feedforward, Left Turns
items.description: Under about 10 mph openpilot's feedforward asks for almost nothing even in a tight turn, so the correction supplies all the torque, late. This adds torque for the wheel angle the turn needs, full under 10 mph and gone by 16 mph. Gentle 40 %, Medium 60 %, Firm 80 %, Full 100 % of a table fitted on your Nov 11 drives (Full never adds more than the gap measured). Off = stock. Not with Lateral Jerk or NNLC.

items.title: Low-Speed Feedforward, Right Turns
items.description: Same as left turns, for right turns. Off on both sides is the feature off.

sections.title: FM Smoothing Settings
sections.description: FM Pilot - calmer steering at low speed and when turns start

items.title: Smooth Turn Start
items.description: Whatever Turn Lead and Turn Hold add on top of the model eases in over about a third of a second instead of arriving all at once, so the steering doesn't grab and then swing back. It still lets go at once, so handing back to the model isn't delayed. The model's own steering is never slowed.

items.title: Low-Speed Correction Strength
items.description: How much of openpilot's low-speed steering correction is kept below about 16 mph (back to normal by 20 mph; highway unchanged). 100 % = stock; lower is calmer: less push to the limit and back mid-turn, but also less torque early in a turn.

items.title: Calmer Crawl-Speed Steering
items.description: Reduces steering requests from action-head models below 5.6 mph. This can calm twitchy steering near a stop and soften the start of tight turns. Off uses the stock floor.

items.title: Calmer Straight Pull-Away
items.description: Reduces steering requests from action-head models when pulling away straight below 5.6 mph. A turn signal, turn request, or sustained steering input brings back the usual steering over half a second. Calmer Crawl-Speed Steering already applies this reduction whenever you are crawling.

sections.title: Model Lateral Smoothing
sections.description: FM Pilot - how much the model's steering request is smoothed, for small and big models

items.title: Small Models
items.description: Model Default uses the model bundle. Higher smoothing makes steering calmer and reads slightly farther ahead in the model plan, so it can steer a little earlier.

items.title: Big Models
items.description: Model Default uses the model’s own behavior. 0.10 s smooths the steering request and can make it respond about 0.1 s later. Prediction timing stays the same.

sections.title: Turns
sections.description: FM Pilot - help through slow blinker turns, before and after them

items.title: Turn Hold
items.description: During a blinker turn under 20 mph, keeps the model from letting go of the turn halfway. Holds the steering request near the turn's strongest point, easing off gradually, until the truck has turned about 75 degrees, the blinker is cancelled, or you steer against the turn. Built in: its 8 seconds only count once the truck is turning; a brief or light press against the turn (under a quarter second and 1.5 Nm, or under 1.5 seconds before the truck has turned 10 degrees, or straightening at the start of a turn under 5 mph) passes through without ending it; it ignores the wheel while openpilot isn't steering; below 5 mph it only holds a request the model kept up for 0.3 seconds; and a deliberate nudge into the turn at 2 to 8 mph adds a little extra steering when the path just ahead already bends that way.

items.title: Turn Lead
items.description: During a blinker turn from Turn Lead Min Speed up to about 16 mph, start turning on time when the model turns in late. Reads the curve of the planned path just ahead and asks for it until the truck catches up, then hands back to the model. Never asks for a tighter turn than Turn Path Tightest Radius. Works with Turn Hold (which then holds what Turn Lead asked for), but using one at a time makes each turn easier to judge. From StarPilot's Model Turn Assist.

items.title: Finish Turn After Signal Cancels
items.description: If the blinker goes off (or cancels itself) early in a turn while the truck is still turning, Turn Lead and Turn Hold keep helping until the truck straightens out, for up to 6 seconds, instead of dropping back to the model at once. Ends right away if you steer against the turn, openpilot stops steering or you reach 20 mph. If the blinker goes off after the truck has turned 45 degrees, or once it is already straightening out, the turn is ending, so Turn Assist lets go over half a second as usual. The model, the Turning alert and lane changes still follow the blinker.

items.title: Hold Path Source
items.description: When starting a turn from a stop or a crawl (under about 2 mph), also take the turn from the planned path, so the truck turns even if the model's steering request still says straight. Never tighter than Turn Path Tightest Radius (12 m unless changed on Turn Lead Settings). From StarPilot's Model Turn Assist.

items.title: Hold Adds Your Steering
items.description: When you steer into the turn, Turn Hold keeps the curve you gave it, up to full lock, instead of letting go and instead of pushing back toward a wider turn, so the help stays once you let go of the wheel. Steering into the turn never releases it, even before the truck starts turning; steering against the turn still releases it. From StarPilot's Model Turn Assist.

items.title: Hold Follows the Model's Exit
items.description: Once the truck has turned 45 degrees, when the model starts letting go of the turn (asking for less than half of the hold's tightest), Turn Hold fades out over half a second so the truck straightens out with the model, instead of holding the turn until 75 degrees. While you press the wheel into the turn it waits until you ease off.

items.title: Stop Before Turning Starts Over
items.description: If the truck stops before it has turned 10 degrees (waiting in a line, creeping up to the stop line), the turn starts over when you pull away. Nothing from the creep carries into the real turn - not Turn Hold's remembered curve, not a hold you released, not Turn Lead paused or switched off by your hands. A turn you pause partway through (past 10 degrees) keeps everything.

items.title: Turn Lead Min Speed
items.description: Lowest speed Turn Lead works at; it reaches full strength about 2 mph above this. Lower it to help turns that start late when pulling away from a stop. 7 mph is about StarPilot's fixed value and the default. Below 2 mph, Turn Hold's Hold Path Source covers turns from a stop.

items.title: Adaptive Look-Ahead
items.description: Reads the path only as far ahead as the steering actually lags, 0.5 s for a gentle curve up to 0.9 s for a tight turn, instead of a fixed 1.3 s, so the turn doesn't start several meters before the corner. Off is the fixed 1.3 s.

items.title: Wait for the Corner
items.description: Turn Lead only starts once the corner is close, within Turn Lead Start Distance, instead of as soon as the planned path shows a turn somewhere ahead. Stops it from turning toward the curb before you reach the corner.

items.title: Turn Lead Start Distance
items.description: With Wait for the Corner, how close the corner has to be (where the planned path has turned 10 degrees, a couple of meters into it) before Turn Lead acts. Smaller starts later. Default 5 m, about 2 to 3 m before the corner.

items.title: Turn Lead Yields to Your Hands
items.description: If you hold the wheel against the turn while Turn Lead is adding steering (a quarter second, or firmly), Turn Lead backs off. Before the truck has turned 10 degrees it only pauses and comes back half a second after you let go; once the truck is turning, it stays off for the rest of that turn. Pressing before Turn Lead starts changes nothing.

items.title: Turn Path Tightest Radius
items.description: The tightest turn Turn Lead may ask for on its own, as a radius. Hold Path Source (Turn Hold Settings) and Turn Hold's built-in nudge share this setting. Smaller is stronger; 8 m is the strongest. Default 12 m. Your own steering (Hold Adds Your Steering) isn't limited by it.

items.title: Queue Guard
items.description: Waiting in a line of cars with the blinker on, the turn normally starts right away, so every creep forward steers toward the turn. With this on, once you are stopped with a car within 8 m ahead, the turn waits (no steering toward it, and the Turning alert goes away) until that car is more than 10 m ahead or gone, or you reach 10 mph; then the turn starts fresh. A turn the truck has already started (10 degrees or more) is never held, and a wait is never taken for the blinker cancelling (Finish Turn After Signal Cancels doesn't carry it).

items.title: Turn Pulse on Pull-Away
items.description: The model only hears a turn for about 5 seconds after it starts, so after a long wait at a corner it has forgotten the turn and turns in late. With this on, when you pull away from a stop with a turn still on, the model is told about the turn again. Only the model's input changes; the turn, its alert and Turn Assist are the same.

items.title: Settle After Turn
items.description: For up to 6 seconds after a blinker turn, between 8 and 30 mph, gently steers toward the middle of the lane using lane lines the model is only 30% sure of, before Blendful or lane centering trust them. After a left turn it only moves away from the center line, never toward it. Road edges only keep it from aiming too close to the curb. It lets go as soon as Blendful takes over, you steer, a new blinker or lane change starts, or you pass 30 mph. When Finish Turn After Signal Cancels carries a turn on, it waits until that carry ends.

items.title: Settle After Turn: Early Right Push
items.description: Needs Settle After Turn. Starts as soon as the truck straightens out of the turn (not only when the blinker goes off), from 3 mph. If no lane line can be seen yet, it eases the truck to the right, at most 0.4 m (about 16 inches), after left and right turns alike, because oncoming traffic is always on the left. It stops when a line shows you are centered or right of center (then it centers as Settle After Turn does), 1.4 m from a sure curb (and steers back left if the path gets too close to it), and holds when the model steers left around something such as a parked car. Your steering cancels it at once. Gentle at low speed. The 3 mph, 0.4 m and strength values are provisional, not yet checked on a recorded drive.

panels.label: Cruise
panels.description: Longitudinal control, speed limits, and cruise behavior

items.title: Disengage Cruise on Accelerator Pedal
items.description: When enabled, pressing the accelerator pedal will disengage longitudinal control.

items.title: Driving Personality
items.description: Standard is recommended. In aggressive mode, sunnypilot will follow lead cars closer and be more aggressive with the gas and brake. In relaxed mode sunnypilot will stay further away from lead cars. On supported cars, you can cycle through these personalities with your steering wheel distance button.

items.title: Accel Boost
items.description: Adds a little acceleration on top of the model's, one kind at a time (FM Pilot). Gas: after you press the gas while the model holds the car below what the lead and set speed allow, adds up to +0.2 m/s² for that engagement (openpilot). Sunny Boost: adds acceleration whenever the model predicts no reason to slow, up to +0.4 / 0.25 / 0.1 m/s² for aggressive / standard / relaxed; fades in tight curves and when the model slows or stops (sunnypilot). EVP Set Speed: above 20 mph, helps the car reach your set speed when only the model holds it back, up to +0.7 / 0.5 / 0.3 m/s²; shrinks as the model slows or the road turns (EVPilot). AP Accel Control: +0.3 / 0.2 / 0.1 m/s² on any model request above 0.1 m/s², from 10 mph, full by 20 mph (AdventurePilot). OP Personality: +0.15 / 0.05 / 0 m/s², faded below 22 mph and when the model brakes (openpilot). The boosts lift only the model's target: the lead and the set speed still limit it. sunnypilot's Acceleration Boost and AP's Acceleration Control toggles are these options now.

items.title: Show Accel Boost On Screen
items.description: Draws a green bar in the side panel of the comma 4 while Accel Boost is on, in place of the confidence ball. It fills with what the boost adds while the boosted model target sets the speed, up to the most the selected boost can add for your driving personality.

items.title: Minimum Stop Distance
items.description: Gap behind a stopped lead car, in tenths of a metre (45 = 4.5 m, 60 = 6.0 m). Default is 60 (6.0 m). Only active when cruise set speed is 50 kph / 31 mph or below; reverts to 6.0 m above that speed. Takes effect after changing from OffRoad to OnRoad.

items.title: Link Stop Distance to Personality
items.description: When enabled, and while the reduced stop distance is active: Aggressive uses the minimum stop distance; Standard uses the midpoint; Relaxed always uses 6.0 m.

items.title: Following Distance Offset
items.description: Scales the time-gap to the lead car across all personality modes (-20% to +20%). Negative values follow closer; positive values follow further. Default is 0 (no change). Takes effect after changing from OffRoad to OnRoad.

sections.title: Speed Limits
sections.description: Speed limit detection and offset behavior

items.title: Ignore Stationary Radar Ghosts
items.description: Never treat a standing-still radar point as the car ahead while the camera sees that car clearly moving (over 11 mph) and not braking hard. Stops guardrails and barriers on ramps and curves from causing sudden braking; the car ahead is then followed from the camera. A car the camera sees braking hard, and anything straight ahead below about 9 mph, still comes from the radar.

items.title: Radar-matched Lead Confidence
items.description: Camera confidence in percent for radar-backed leads. Radar matching starts above the lower of the two lead confidence settings. Lower values can pick up cars earlier and can admit false leads. Default 50% (stock). From FrogPilot.

items.title: Camera-only Lead Confidence
items.description: Minimum camera confidence in percent to follow without a radar match. Default 50% (stock).

items.title: Smooth Lead Handoffs
items.description: Ease brake release when radar and camera switch on the same car, and briefly keep tracking it when radar drops.

items.title: Vision
items.description: Use vision path predictions to estimate the appropriate speed to drive through turns ahead.

items.title: Map
items.description: Use map data to estimate the appropriate speed to drive through turns ahead.

items.title: Curve
items.description: Slow down ahead of curves and power smoothly through them, keeping cornering within the steering's limits. Uses the vision path; no map data required.

panels.label: Display
panels.description: Screen brightness, timeout, and interactivity settings

sections.title: Brightness & Timeout
sections.description: Screen dimming and sleep behavior while driving

items.title: Interactivity Timeout
items.description: Apply a custom timeout for settings UI. This is the time after which settings UI closes automatically if user is not interacting with the screen.

items.title: Screen Saver
items.description: Show a screen saver when the device is offroad and idle, instead of turning the screen off.

items.title: Screen Saver Duration
items.description: How long the screen saver runs before the screen turns off.

items.title: Screen Saver Text
items.description: Choose what the screen saver shows. Custom text and logos are set up on the device itself, and are not available on the comma 4.

items.title: Custom Text
items.description: The text shown when Custom is selected. Type it on the device, under Display settings.

items.title: Screen Saver Logo
items.description: The image shown when Logo is selected. Upload and choose it on the device, under Display settings.

panels.label: Visuals
panels.description: HUD overlays, alerts, and on-screen display elements

sections.title: HUD Elements
sections.description: Overlays shown on the driving screen

items.title: Show Blind Spot Warnings
items.description: Enabling this will display warnings when a vehicle is detected in your blind spot as long as your car has BSM supported.

items.title: Steering Arc
items.description: Display steering arc on the driving screen when lateral control is enabled.

items.title: Display Turn Signals
items.description: When enabled, visual turn indicators are drawn on the HUD.

items.title: Display Road Name
items.description: Displays the name of the road the car is traveling on. The OpenStreetMap database of the location must be downloaded to fetch the road name.

items.title: Standstill Timer
items.description: Show a timer on the HUD when the car is at a standstill.

items.title: Real-time Acceleration Bar
items.description: Show an indicator on the left side of the screen to display real-time vehicle acceleration and deceleration. This displays what the car is currently doing, not what the planner is requesting.

sections.title: Developer UI Info
sections.description: Speedometer and debug display options

items.title: Developer UI
items.description: Display real-time parameters and metrics from various sources.

items.title: Speedometer: Always Display True Speed
items.description: For applicable vehicles, always display the true vehicle current speed from wheel speed sensors.

items.title: Speedometer: Hide from Onroad Screen
items.description: When enabled, the speedometer on the onroad screen is not displayed.

sections.title: Alerts & Extras
sections.description: Traffic light alerts and visual flair

items.title: Green Traffic Light Alert (Beta)
items.description: A chime and on-screen alert will play when the traffic light you are waiting for turns green and you have no vehicle in front of you. On-screen visual alert is only available on comma 3X. Note: This chime is only designed as a notification. It is the driver's responsibility to observe their environment and make decisions accordingly.

items.title: Lead Departure Alert (Beta)
items.description: A chime and on-screen alert will play when you are stopped, and the vehicle in front of you start moving. On-screen visual alert is only available on comma 3X. Note: This chime is only designed as a notification. It is the driver's responsibility to observe their environment and make decisions accordingly.

items.title: Tesla Rainbow Mode
items.description: Display a rainbow effect on the path the model wants to take. It does not affect driving in any way.

items.title: Enable sunnypilot
items.description: Use the sunnypilot system for adaptive cruise control and lane keep driver assistance. Your attention is required at all times to use this feature.

items.title: Enable Lane Departure Warnings
items.description: Receive alerts to steer back into the lane when your vehicle drifts over a detected lane line without a turn signal activated while driving over 31 mph (50 km/h).

items.title: Always-On Driver Monitoring
items.description: Enable driver monitoring even when sunnypilot is not engaged.

items.title: Use Metric System
items.description: Display speed in km/h instead of mph.

sections.title: Recording
sections.description: Camera and audio recording during drives

items.title: Record and Upload Driver Camera
items.description: Upload data from the driver facing camera and help improve the driver monitoring algorithm.

items.title: Record and Upload Microphone Audio
items.description: Record and store microphone audio while driving. The audio will be included in the dashcam video in comma connect.

panels.label: Device
panels.description: Device behavior, units, and recording settings

sections.title: General
sections.description: Power, boot, and unit preferences

items.title: Wake Up Behavior
items.description: Controls state of the device after boot/sleep. Default: Device will boot/wake-up normally and will be ready to engage. Offroad: Device will be in Always Offroad mode after boot/wake-up.

items.title: Max Time Offroad
items.description: Device will automatically shutdown after set time once the engine is turned off. 30h is the default.

items.title: Jetlink (Experimental)
items.description: Runs the big driving model on a Jetson, Mac or Linux PC (USB), or an iPhone/iPad (iOS), plugged into the comma's USB-C port with a USB 3 cable. Power the comma from the car, not that port. If the link drops, the comma keeps driving on the small model. Not used when a chestnut is fitted. Also on the device under Models.

sections.title: Updates
sections.description: Control software updates

items.title: Disable Updates
items.description: When enabled, software updates will be off. This requires a reboot to take effect.

panels.label: Developer
panels.description: Debug tools, remote access, and advanced services

sections.title: Connectivity
sections.description: Remote access and debugging interfaces

items.title: Enable ADB
items.description: ADB (Android Debug Bridge) allows connecting to your device over USB or over the network. See https://docs.comma.ai/how-to/connect-to-comma for more info.

items.title: sunnypilot Longitudinal Control (Alpha)
items.description: WARNING: sunnypilot longitudinal control is in alpha for this car and will disable Automatic Emergency Braking (AEB). On this car, sunnypilot defaults to the car's built-in ACC instead of sunnypilot's longitudinal control. Enable this to switch to sunnypilot longitudinal control. Enabling Experimental mode is recommended when enabling sunnypilot longitudinal control alpha. Changing this setting will restart sunnypilot if the car is powered on.

items.title: Navigation (Alpha)
items.description: Turn-by-turn navigation with a route map. Set a destination from comma connect.

sections.title: Test Maneuvers
sections.description: DANGER: enabling these maneuvers replaces normal driving behavior with deterministic test sequences. Each toggle requires explicit confirmation per write. Use only in a closed environment.

items.title: [TEST] Lateral Maneuver Mode
items.description: Replaces normal lateral control with a deterministic test sequence. NOT for road use.

items.title: [TEST] Longitudinal Maneuver Mode
items.description: Replaces normal longitudinal control with a deterministic test sequence. NOT for road use.

items.title: Show Advanced Controls
items.description: Toggle visibility of advanced sunnypilot controls. This only changes the visibility of the toggles; it does not change the actual enabled/disabled state.

items.title: GitHub Runner Service
items.description: Enables or disables the GitHub runner service.

items.title: copyparty Service
items.description: copyparty is a very capable file server, you can use it to download your routes, view your logs and even make some edits on some files from your browser. Requires you to connect to your comma locally via its IP address.

panels.label: Models
panels.description: Driving model behavior and camera calibration

sections.title: Model Behavior
sections.description: Lane desire and lead-vehicle awareness tuning (FM Pilot - Blendful is picked under Steering > Lane Centering)

items.title: Use Lane Turn Desires
items.description: If you are driving at 20 mph (32 km/h) or below and have your blinker on, the car will plan a turn in that direction at the nearest drivable path. This prevents situations (like at red lights) where the car might plan the wrong turn direction.

items.title: Adjust Lane Turn Speed
items.description: Set the maximum speed for lane turn desires.

items.title: Live Learning Steer Delay
items.description: Allow device to learn and adapt car's steering response time

items.title: Adjust Software Delay
items.description: Adjust the software delay when Live Learning Steer Delay is toggled off. The default software delay value is 0.2

sections.title: Lateral Control
sections.description: Neural network lateral control for supported models

items.title: Neural Network Lateral Control (NNLC)
items.description: Use a neural network for lateral control instead of the default torque controller.

sections.title: Camera
sections.description: Camera position and calibration

items.title: Adjust Camera Offset
items.description: Virtually shift camera's perspective to move model's center to Left(+ values) or Right (- values)

items.title: Rivian: Enable Resume
items.description: When enabled a full stalk down action held for at least 0.5s, provided activation of ACC is available on stock Rivian, will set the cruise speed to be equal to that from the last time cruise was deactivated. If cruise has never been activated it will set the cruise speed to the current vehicle speed. It is recommended to disable the stock Rivian feature: "Set to speed limit on divided highways", which uses the same activation mechanism.

items.title: Rear-Axle Off-Tracking Compensation
items.description: Widens tight turns so the rear wheels, which cut inside the front wheels' path on a long wheelbase, are less likely to clip a curb. A geometric estimate from the wheelbase (3.45 m on an R1T, 3.08 m on an R1S, read from the VIN), not curb sensing. Off by default.

items.title: Stop and Go for Manual Parking Brake (Beta)
MADS Screen Activation
items.description: Use a multi-finger press on the infotainment screen to toggle MADS. This allows the use of full MADS functionality when enabled. Selecting a higher finger count may reduce accidental activations. Note: Setting this to Off will reset your MADS settings to default.

items.title: Enforce Factory Longitudinal Control
items.description: sunnypilot will not take over control of gas and brakes. Factory Toyota longitudinal control will be used.

items.title: Stop and Go Hack (Alpha)
items.description: sunnypilot will allow some Toyota/Lexus cars to auto resume during stop and go traffic. This feature is only applicable to certain models that are able to use longitudinal control. This is an alpha feature. Use at your own risk.

items.title: TSS2 Smooth Longitudinal (Alpha)
items.description: Enable smoother longitudinal control for TSS2 vehicles. Uses a custom speed-dependent integral gain curve for smoother traffic driving.
